themeDescription: Communities, systems, and how we live together

days.title: Turning Food Into Fuel
days.learning_objective: Turning Food Into Fuel is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Explain how telescopes gather light to view distant objects.
Identify and differentiate between refracting and reflecting telescopes.
Describe the impact of telescopes on our understanding of the universe.

days.title: Getting Rid of Waste
days.learning_objective: Getting Rid of Waste is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of a microscope and explain their functions.
Prepare a wet mount slide and observe a specimen under a microscope.
Explain how microscopes have contributed to scientific discoveries.

days.title: From One Cell to Trillions
days.learning_objective: Cell division multiplies cells to build complex organisms.
learning_objectives: Define an ecosystem and identify its key components (biotic and abiotic).
Describe the flow of energy through a food chain and food web.
Explain how different organisms interact within an ecosystem (e.g., predator-prey, symbiotic relationships).
Identify the major types of ecosystems (e.g., forest, grassland, aquatic).

days.title: How Bodies Fix Themselves
days.learning_objective: Understanding how bodies fix themselves helps us make sense of the world.
learning_objectives: Define and identify the roles of producers, consumers, and decomposers in a food chain.
Construct simple food chains, accurately representing energy flow from one organism to another.
Explain the importance of each organism in maintaining a balanced ecosystem.

days.title: Animals That Hunt
days.learning_objective: Animals That Hunt is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three different predator animals and their habitats.
Explain how predators obtain food by hunting other animals.
Describe at least two adaptations that help predators survive.

days.title: Animals That Get Hunted
days.learning_objective: Animals That Get Hunted is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define 'prey' and provide examples of prey animals.
Identify at least three different survival strategies used by prey animals.
Explain the importance of prey animals within their ecosystems.

days.title: Hiding in Plain Sight
days.learning_objective: Camouflage helps animals blend into their environment.
learning_objectives: Define the term "herbivore" and identify examples of herbivorous animals.
Describe the adaptations that herbivores have to digest plant matter.
Explain the role of herbivores in a food chain or food web.

days.title: Looking Like Something Else
days.learning_objective: Looking Like Something Else is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define 'carnivore' and identify examples of carnivorous animals.
Explain the role of carnivores in a food chain.
Describe at least three adaptations that help carnivores hunt and eat meat.

days.title: Species That Help Each Other
days.learning_objective: Species That Help Each Other is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify at least 5 different omnivorous animals.
Explain the difference between herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores.
Describe the role of omnivores in a food web.

days.title: Living Off Others
days.learning_objective: Living Off Others is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the major types of decomposers (fungi, bacteria, invertebrates).
Explain the process of decomposition and its role in nutrient cycling.
Describe the importance of decomposers for maintaining healthy ecosystems.

days.title: Nature's Cleanup Crew
days.learning_objective: Nature's Cleanup Crew is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define photosynthesis and its role in plant life.
Identify the key ingredients needed for photosynthesis.
Explain how plants convert sunlight into sugar (glucose).
Describe the importance of photosynthesis for the environment.
Recognize the relationship between plants, sunlight, and oxygen production.

days.title: Who Eats Whom
days.learning_objective: Who Eats Whom is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Explain the process of respiration in living cells.
Identify the reactants and products of aerobic respiration.
Compare and contrast aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

days.title: Nature's Connected Eating
days.learning_objective: Nature's Connected Eating is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define adaptation and provide examples.
Students will be able to differentiate between physical and behavioral adaptations.
Students will be able to analyze how specific adaptations help organisms survive in their environments.

days.title: Energy Moving Through Life
days.learning_objective: Energy transforms from one form to another but never disappears.
learning_objectives: Define camouflage and explain its purpose for survival.
Identify and differentiate between various types of camouflage (e.g., crypsis, mimicry, disruptive coloration).
Provide examples of animals and plants that use camouflage in different environments.

days.title: Earth's Different Zones
days.learning_objective: Climate zones divide Earth into regions with distinct weather patterns.
learning_objectives: Define mimicry and differentiate between Batesian and Müllerian mimicry.
Identify examples of mimicry in both plants and animals.
Explain the evolutionary advantages of mimicry for survival.

days.title: Why Variety Matters
days.learning_objective: Understanding why variety matters matters to us and the world.
learning_objectives: Define migration and identify its primary drivers (food and better conditions).
Describe at least three different examples of animal migration.
Explain the challenges and adaptations associated with migration.

days.title: Outsiders Taking Over
days.learning_objective: Outsiders Taking Over is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three animals that hibernate.
Explain the purpose of hibernation as an energy-saving adaptation.
Describe the physical changes that occur in an animal's body during hibernation.

days.title: Who Belongs Where
days.learning_objective: Who Belongs Where is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the four stages of complete metamorphosis.
Describe the key physical changes that occur during each stage of metamorphosis.
Explain the advantages of metamorphosis for the survival of certain species.

days.title: Animals That Hold It Together
days.learning_objective: Animals That Hold It Together is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify the basic stages of life cycles in plants and animals.
Describe the differences between various life cycles (e.g., butterfly vs. frog).
Explain how environmental factors can affect life cycles.

days.title: How Life Makes More Life
days.learning_objective: Reproduction creates new generations of living things.
learning_objectives: Define reproduction and explain its importance for species survival.
Compare and contrast sexual and asexual reproduction.
Identify examples of diverse reproductive strategies in different organisms.

days.title: The Code of Life
days.learning_objective: Code of Life plays an important role in how the world works.
learning_objectives: Define genetics and heredity.
Identify the roles of DNA, genes, and chromosomes.
Explain how traits are passed from parents to offspring.

days.title: What You Get From Parents
days.learning_objective: Understanding what you get from parents reveals about our world.
learning_objectives: Define DNA and describe its basic structure (double helix, nucleotides, bases).
Explain the role of DNA in heredity and how traits are passed from parents to offspring.
Identify real-world applications of DNA technology, such as genetic testing and forensics.

days.title: Why Everyone's Different
days.learning_objective: Understanding why everyone's different matters to us and the world.
learning_objectives: Define evolution and explain its gradual nature over generations.
Identify and describe key mechanisms of evolution, including natural selection and genetic variation.
Analyze real-world examples of evolution and its impact on biodiversity.

days.title: How Nature Chooses
days.learning_objective: Understanding how nature chooses helps us make sense of the world.
learning_objectives: Define extinction and identify its causes.
Name at least three extinct animal species and describe their habitats.
Explain the difference between natural extinction and human-caused extinction.
Identify actions that can be taken to protect endangered species.

days.title: Animals Running Out of Time
days.learning_objective: Time passes at a constant rate, yet feels different in different moments.
learning_objectives: Define 'endangered species' and identify factors contributing to their endangerment.
Explain the importance of biodiversity and the role endangered species play in ecosystems.
Research and present information about a specific endangered species, including its habitat, threats, and conservation efforts.

days.title: Places Species Call Home
days.learning_objective: Habitats provide the conditions species need to survive.
learning_objectives: Define conservation and explain its importance.
Identify different types of natural resources and how they are used.
Describe at least three ways to conserve natural resources in daily life.

days.title: Stuff in the Wrong Place
days.learning_objective: Stuff in the Wrong Place is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Define pollution and identify different types of pollution (air, water, land).
Explain the sources and causes of pollution, both natural and human-induced.
Describe the harmful effects of pollution on the environment, human health, and animal welfare.

days.title: Things That Grow Back
days.learning_objective: Regeneration allows some organisms to regrow lost parts.
learning_objectives: Define recycling and explain its purpose.
Identify common recyclable materials.
Describe the steps involved in the recycling process.

days.title: Things That Run Out
days.learning_objective: Things That Run Out is an important concept that helps us understand our world.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three different sources of renewable energy.
Explain how renewable energy sources are replenished naturally.
Describe the benefits of using renewable energy over fossil fuels.

days.title: Power From the Sun
days.learning_objective: The Sun provides energy for almost all life on Earth.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to explain the basic process of converting sunlight into electricity.
Students will be able to identify at least three advantages of using solar power compared to fossil fuels.
Students will be able to describe at least one real-world application of solar power technology.
